Could you give us a quick rough-cut estimate of required tokens/sec at peak, and a suggested Dedicated pool (GPU counts/types) to meet the SLO with ~1.5x headroom? Also tell us trade-offs for cost vs. headroom (e.g., burst vs. reserved). We want this for the internal procurement deck by Friday.

Hi Sana —

Thanks for the details. Below is a concise, traceable estimate you can drop into the procurement deck. I built this as a conservative "peak-hour" model and included choices for latency-first (higher headroom) vs cost-first (smaller reserved + burst). See attached spreadsheet for the per-GPU sims.

Summary numbers (assumptions):
- Daily requests = MAU*prompts_per_user = 100k * 3 = 300k requests/day
- Avg tokens/request = 40 (input) + 160 (generation) = 200 tokens/request
- Daily tokens = 300k * 200 = 60,000,000 tokens/day
- Peak hour share = 20% of daily tokens (conservative) => 12,000,000 tokens in peak hour
- Peak tokens/sec = 12,000,000 / 3600 ≈ 3,333 tokens/sec

Model throughput mapping (empirical runbook + Redwood runtime assumptions):
- H100 (single contiguous inference slice, optimized kernels + q4f16): ~9,000 tokens/sec (batching + KV caching not assumed)
- A100 80GB equiv (well-tuned): ~3,800 tokens/sec
- GPU baseline for smaller instance-class (T4/A10-like): ~650 tokens/sec

Sizing recommendations to meet 95p < 450ms and ~1.5x headroom:
Option A (latency-first, fewer machines, more expensive):
- 1 x H100 (9k t/s) covers peak 3.3k t/s with ~2.7x headroom. Good headroom for concurrency and model overhead.
- Add 1 standby H100 (or configured burst on Dedicated pool) for maintenance and failover.
- Autoscale policy: keep 1 reserved H100, enable burst to second H100 when sustained usage >60% for 5 minutes.

Option B (cost-balanced, multiple smaller GPUs):
- 2 x A100-equivalent (each ~3.8k t/s) => combined ~7.6k t/s with ~2.3x headroom. Better parallelization for different model variants.
- Add small T4/A10 nodes for background workloads / cheaper baseline, and route latency-sensitive traffic to A100/H100 lane.

Option C (commit-light, burst-heavy):
- 1 x A100 reserved (~3.8k t/s) + burst capacity on Hosted pool for peaks (H100 spot bursts). Headroom ~1.1x for reserved portion — requires stricter rate-limiting or graceful degradation for large peaks.

Notes on SLO fit and latency:
- The 95p <450ms target depends heavily on prompt/response token length and whether streaming is acceptable. Our latency numbers above assume non-streaming end-to-end generation; switching to streaming can reduce perceived tail latency even if token throughput is high.
- KV/prefix caching (if many repeated prompts) can reduce effective tokens/sec significantly; we can model that if you share a sample cache hit-rate.
- Quantization (q4f16/q5) and kernel fusion on H100 materially increase tokens/sec; the H100 number above assumes aggressive kernel selection.

Operational controls we recommend:
- Canary rollout: route 10% of production traffic to the Dedicated pool for 48hrs after initial launch.
- Rate limit spikes with graceful fallback to a cheaper model for non-critical requests.
- Reserve a maintenance/standby machine for patching windows.

Next actions needed from Omega for final reserved sizing & pricing:
1) Confirm target commit window (12/24/36 months) and whether burst pool credit is acceptable.
2) Share a 24-hr sample of request timestamps and a small prompt corpus (we can run a cache-hit sim).
3) Indicate whether streaming UI is required (changes latency mapping).

I attached the detailed per-GPU calculator (omega-sizing-v1.xlsx) + a simple diagram of expected tail latency under each option. Happy to jump on a quick call tomorrow to walk through the numbers.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
(Attachment: omega-sizing-v1.xlsx, slo-latency-diagrams.pdf)
